hyperedges.label: Persistence Ceiling: Measurement to Proposed Fixes

nodes.label: Compare what Redis says about a poll with what PostgreSQL actually stored.…
nodes.norm_label: compare what redis says about a poll with what postgresql actually stored....

nodes.label: Vote API Throughput Plateau (12-13k/s)
nodes.rationale: From 50 connections up throughput flattens at 12-13k votes/s (CPU-bound, and the generator shares the CPU so this is a lower bound); latency grows linearly to p50 40 ms at 500 connections with zero non-2xx.

nodes.label: Server-Side Vote Conservation Check
nodes.rationale: Redis voters set (347,142) equalled PostgreSQL rows (26,496) plus vote:queue depth (320,646), proving no votes were lost inside Redis itself.

nodes.label: W7 Confirmed: Persistence Ceiling
nodes.rationale: 346,636 votes accepted in 30 s with 0 non-2xx while the worker saved exactly 1,000 votes every ~5.1 s (~195/s): the HTTP layer is ~59x faster than the path to PostgreSQL, so the backlog is also the window of exposure to Redis data loss (W5).

nodes.label: Independent curl Latency Probe
nodes.rationale: autocannon reported p50 139 ms at 10 connections and 11.5k/s, which is arithmetically impossible, so user-facing latency is taken from a separate curl probe run alongside each stage; autocannon's reported 'errors' were end-of-stage socket errors, not HTTP failures.

nodes.label: Datasource Configuration (env-only)
nodes.rationale: url/username/password have no default values, so an unset SPRING_DATASOURCE_* variable aborts startup instead of silently using a committed credential.

nodes.label: Actuator Health Exposure Configuration
nodes.rationale: Only the health endpoint is exposed over the web and show-details defaults to never, so dependency internals stay hidden unless HEALTH_SHOW_DETAILS=always is set locally.

nodes.label: spring.data.redis Configuration
nodes.rationale: Keys live under spring.data.redis because Spring Boot 3+ stopped binding spring.redis, while SPRING_REDIS_HOST/PORT/PASSWORD/SSL names are preserved with localhost:6379 defaults.

nodes.label: Persistence Ceiling (Confirmed Bottleneck)
nodes.rationale: VoteFlushWorker saves ~200 votes/s while the API accepts ~12-13k/s, so vote:queue grows without bound. Causes: one LPOP per vote, saveAll with GenerationType.IDENTITY disabling Hibernate batching, and a fixed 5 s delay between flushes.

nodes.label: Whole-Batch Re-Queue Poisoning
nodes.rationale: A failed batch is re-queued whole, so a single duplicate row can make the same batch fail on every retry attempt.

nodes.label: Queued Votes Lost if Redis Dies
nodes.norm_label: queued votes lost if redis dies
nodes.rationale: LPOP removes a vote from vote:queue before the database commit, so the in-flight window has no durable copy anywhere.

nodes.label: Committed Supabase Password Needs Rotation
nodes.rationale: The password was committed in earlier revisions of application.yaml; removing it from the file does not remove it from git history, so it must be rotated in Supabase.

nodes.label: Feature Register
nodes.rationale: A single append-only list (date, status, touched files, one-line summary) exists so a future agent can find the current state of every feature in one place instead of reading history.

nodes.label: Main Runtime Vote Flow
nodes.rationale: PollController -> VoteService (rate limit, poll state, expiry) -> RedisVoteService (duplicate check, counter increment) -> vote:queue -> VoteFlushWorker -> PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Measured Performance (2026-09-22)
nodes.rationale: Vote API plateaus at ~12-13k votes/s; VoteFlushWorker drains at ~200 votes/s (~60x slower), so 2.5 minutes of load left 1,826,851 votes queued, ~152 minutes from PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Agent Handoff Payload
nodes.rationale: Goal, files touched, behavior rules, validation performed and open risks - the minimum a new agent needs without replaying the chat.

nodes.label: /actuator/health Dependency Reporting
nodes.rationale: Reports db, redis and voteQueue (pendingVotes) separately so an operator can tell which dependency is degraded; /health alone only proves the process is up.

nodes.label: Resume Procedure for Interrupted Groups
nodes.rationale: Start postgresql@14, delete results/B-E and .run, launch the four group scripts in parallel with nohup, then A4-A6, then write REPORT.md from FINDINGS.md; scripts must run under bash, not zsh.

nodes.label: Test Groups A-E and Phase Status
nodes.norm_label: test groups a-e and phase status
nodes.rationale: A1 baseline and A2 ramp are done; A3 sustained was skipped because A2 already demonstrated unbounded queue growth; A4-A6 are todo and B-E were interrupted 2026-09-22 01:45 and need a clean re-run with partial output deleted.

nodes.label: Failure Scenarios Playbook
nodes.rationale: Seven scenarios (Redis unreachable, partial Redis writes, queue backlog, PostgreSQL down, duplicate rows, worker crash, rate-limiter false positives) each mapped symptoms -> immediate actions -> remediation -> prevention; the overriding rule is never to purge vote:queue.

nodes.label: Monitoring and Alert Thresholds
nodes.rationale: Alert when LLEN vote:queue > 10k for over 5 minutes, on RedisUnavailableException spikes, on 5xx rate above 1%, and track vote endpoint p95/p99 latency.

nodes.label: AI Context Management Folder
nodes.rationale: The folder is a lightweight memory layer; entries stay short because the goal is stable context, not long chat transcripts.

nodes.label: HELP.md Spring Boot Getting Started
nodes.rationale: Generated starter references for Spring Web, Spring Data Redis and Spring Data JPA, plus a note that the POM carries empty license/developers overrides to block unwanted parent inheritance.

nodes.label: Decision: Actuator Health Checks with Hidden Details
nodes.norm_label: decision: actuator health checks with hidden details
nodes.rationale: db, redis and voteQueue indicators were added, but show-details defaults to never (HEALTH_SHOW_DETAILS=always opts in) so a public server does not expose internal dependency state.

nodes.label: Decision: Commit Directly to main (No Pull Requests)
nodes.norm_label: decision: commit directly to main (no pull requests)

nodes.label: Decision: Standardize Context on .ai Folder plus AGENTS.md
nodes.norm_label: decision: standardize context on .ai folder plus agents.md
nodes.rationale: A small .ai folder plus AGENTS.md keeps stable project knowledge in one place so new agents do not rediscover the system each session; secret values were explicitly excluded from that knowledge because they belong in environment configuration.

nodes.label: Decision: Remove Credential Fallbacks from application.yaml
nodes.norm_label: decision: remove credential fallbacks from application.yaml
nodes.rationale: Hardcoded datasource and Redis credential fallbacks were removed so secrets come only from environment variables (template in .env.example) and startup fails fast when datasource values are absent.

nodes.label: Decision: Remove k6 Load Testing
nodes.rationale: scripts/k6/vote_test.js and its RUNBOOK references were deleted because k6 is no longer part of the project's tooling; load testing later reappeared as the resilience-tests harness.

nodes.label: Decision: Commit Resilience Scripts, Ignore Per-Run Output
nodes.norm_label: decision: commit resilience scripts, ignore per-run output
nodes.rationale: Scripts and findings are committed while results/, .run/ and node_modules/ are git-ignored because every run regenerates them; measured numbers are recorded in the brief and FINDINGS.md so agents do not re-measure before touching the vote path.

nodes.label: Decision: Move Redis Config to spring.data.redis.*
nodes.norm_label: decision: move redis config to spring.data.redis.*
nodes.rationale: Spring Boot 3+ no longer binds spring.redis.*, so the keys moved to spring.data.redis.* while the existing SPRING_REDIS_* environment variable names were deliberately kept to avoid breaking deployments.

nodes.label: Fix: Bulk LPOP + JDBC Batch Insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
nodes.norm_label: fix: bulk lpop + jdbc batch insert with on conflict do nothing
nodes.rationale: Named as the first fix because it attacks all three measured causes at once: per-vote LPOP, disabled Hibernate batching, and the fixed inter-flush delay (drain until empty).

nodes.label: Fix: Move vote:queue to Redis Streams
nodes.norm_label: fix: move vote:queue to redis streams
nodes.rationale: XADD/XREADGROUP/XACK keeps an unacknowledged entry in the stream until it is committed, so votes survive a crash instead of vanishing with the LPOP.

nodes.label: Invariant: Redis-First Vote Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Redis is the first source for live acceptance and counting, duplicates stay blocked per poll and user, rate limiting runs before processing, inactive or expired polls are rejected, and async DB persistence must never break the live count path.

nodes.label: Stable Editing Rule: Prefer Narrow Fixes
nodes.norm_label: stable editing rule: prefer narrow fixes
nodes.rationale: A small fix in the owning service or worker is preferred over a broad refactor because Redis and PostgreSQL behavior must be reconciled carefully whenever vote or queue logic changes.

nodes.label: Rule: Mirror Feature Changes into .ai Files
nodes.norm_label: rule: mirror feature changes into .ai files
nodes.rationale: Any agent that adds, changes or removes a feature must update project-brief.md and decision-log.md in the same change, and known-issues.md when follow-up work remains, so the context packet cannot drift from the code.

nodes.label: Rule: Preserve the Core Voting Flow
nodes.norm_label: rule: preserve the core voting flow
nodes.rationale: Redis first, duplicate vote prevention, rate limiting and async persistence are called out as non-negotiable, and focused changes must be validated before scope expands.

nodes.label: Asynchronous Vote Persistence (Redis to PostgreSQL)
nodes.rationale: Vote events are queued in Redis (vote:queue) and written to PostgreSQL by a scheduled worker in batches so the live vote path never waits on a database commit; durability is traded for low-latency acceptance.

nodes.label: Duplicate Vote Prevention via Redis Set
nodes.norm_label: duplicate vote prevention via redis set
nodes.rationale: A Redis Set (SADD on poll:{pollId}:voters) is used because the operation is atomic and O(1), so one voter can be rejected on a second vote without a database round trip on the hot path.

nodes.label: Environment-Variable Startup Contract
nodes.rationale: No credentials live in application.yaml; the app fails fast at startup if SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL/USERNAME/PASSWORD are missing, so a misconfigured deploy cannot silently fall back to a committed default.

nodes.label: Kafka for Durable Replayable Event Streaming
nodes.norm_label: kafka for durable replayable event streaming
nodes.rationale: Proposed replacement for the Redis list queue because a Redis LPOP queue loses everything queued if Redis dies and cannot be replayed.

nodes.label: Poll Expiration Handling
nodes.rationale: Polls are auto-closed by a scheduled worker and also re-validated at vote time, so a vote cannot slip through in the window between expiry and the worker's next sweep.

nodes.label: Run Heavy Load Against Local PostgreSQL, Not Supabase
nodes.norm_label: run heavy load against local postgresql, not supabase
nodes.rationale: Supabase free-tier limits would distort results, so heavy runs use a local PostgreSQL 14 voting_test database and local Redis 8 for clean numbers; Supabase is kept as a separate A6 comparison.

nodes.label: Prevention: Atomic Lua Script for addVoter + increment
nodes.norm_label: prevention: atomic lua script for addvoter + increment
nodes.rationale: SADD and INCR are individually atomic but not atomic together, so a partial write leaves a voter recorded with no counter increment; a Lua script would make the pair indivisible.

nodes.label: Prevention: Idempotent DB Inserts (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)
nodes.norm_label: prevention: idempotent db inserts (on conflict do nothing)
nodes.rationale: Replaying the queue after an outage can re-insert the same vote, so batch inserts should swallow conflicts instead of failing, backed by the unique constraint on vote(user_id, poll_id).

nodes.label: Redis Key Conventions
nodes.rationale: poll:{pollId}:option:{optionId} counter, poll:{pollId}:voters duplicate-blocking set, poll:{pollId}:options valid-option set (rebuilt from DB if missing), vote:queue entries as pollId:userId:optionId, and rate_limit:{userId}.

nodes.label: Decision: Validate Vote Options from a Redis Option Set
nodes.norm_label: decision: validate vote options from a redis option set
nodes.rationale: Validation is backed by a Redis set per poll (poll:{pollId}:options) with DB fallback so the check costs one extra Redis call rather than a database query per vote; invalid options return 400.

nodes.label: Per-User Rate Limiting with Redis INCR + EXPIRE
nodes.norm_label: per-user rate limiting with redis incr + expire
nodes.rationale: INCR plus EXPIRE on rate_limit:{userId} gives a cheap fixed-window counter that expires itself, avoiding any separate cleanup job or state store for abuse prevention.
